unknowns: is_edible left null: neither the NC State page nor the RHS page addresses eating or culinary/food use of Marsh Fern anywhere.
Checked NC State and RHS pages for 'Poison', 'Toxic', and 'Problem for' -- zero hits on both pages; no toxicity information found on either anchor page.

Size comes from NC State's page for Thelypteris palustris subsp. pubescens (eastern marsh fern; 'Previously known as: Thelypteris palustris var. pubescens'), the North American subspecies of this species -- the page gives its range as eastern Canada and the USA, Bermuda, Cuba and parts of Mexico. A subspecies is a wild population of the species itself, not a cultivar, so its Dimensions block is used for Thelypteris palustris: Height 1-3 ft (12-36 in) and Width 2-3 ft (24-36 in). These are broadly consistent with RHS's page for the species as a whole, Max Height/Max Spread of 0.5-1 metres (about 19.7-39.4 in), so no conflict was resolved by preference (corrected at landing: the note had called the NC State page species-specific).

NC State's Wildlife Value text ('Only known host for the Marsh Fern Moth (Fagitana littera). Small mammals browse the foliage.') was not used to support attracts_pollinators -- small mammals browsing foliage is not pollination per the rules; the Moths entry in the structured Attracts field was used instead.
This is not a climber (NC State Plant Type: Fern, Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial), so all four size fields were populated normally per the rules.

RHS page was searched for 'Ultimate height', 'Attracts', 'Edible', 'Poison', 'Toxic', 'Problem for', 'Pollinator', and 'pollinators' -- zero hits on all of these; RHS's only relevant field found was the Max Height/Max Spread size block, which was not needed since NC State (the species-specific anchor) already carries size.

attracts_pollinators removed on audit: The only support is the bare word 'Moths' in NC State's Attracts field (listed next to 'Small Mammals'). The same NC State page says, under Flower Description, 'No flowers.' and, under Fruit Description, 'No fruits. This plants reproduces via spores.' Its Wildlife Value explains why moths are listed: 'Only known host for the Marsh Fern Moth (Fagitana littera).' The tags also include '#moth caterpillar host' and '#larval host plant'. So the moths are there as larvae feeding on the fronds, not as pollinators. A fern with no flowers cannot be pollinated. The researcher's unknowns set the Wildlife Value text aside, but that text is exactly what the 'Moths' entry means. RHS has zero hits for 'Pollinat' and describes propagation 'by division or spores'. This is Check E: larval-host and wildlife-value support that names no pollinator. The field should be null, not true.

landed.summary: I re-read both pages with qc.py. The four size values hold up: NC State says Height 1-3 ft and Width 2-3 ft, which correctly become 12-36 in and 24-36 in. The quotes are verbatim single runs, and the RHS species page (0.5-1 m for both height and spread) agrees roughly. It is not a climber. One caveat: the NC State page is for subsp. pubescens, not the species as the unknowns claim. It is a subspecies, not a cultivar, and it agrees with RHS, so the sizes stand. is_edible is correctly null because both pages say nothing about eating or toxicity. attracts_pollinators=true is refuted. The 'Moths' entry reflects the plant being the larval host of the Marsh Fern Moth (Fagitana littera), and the same NC State page states 'No flowers.' and that it reproduces via spores. A flowerless fern cannot attract pollinators, so the field should be null.

landed.summary: I re-read all three pages with qc.py and none of the six proposed values is refuted. On the NC State species page, the lines 'Height: 5 ft. 0 in. - 6 ft. 0 in.' and 'Width: 2 ft. 0 in. - 3 ft. 0 in.' each sit on one rendered line, and they convert correctly to 60-72 and 24-36 inches. None of the size values is a feet figure left unconverted. The plant is a herbaceous perennial fern, not a climber, the figures belong to the species rather than a cultivar, and the citation labels contain the field names. is_edible and attracts_pollinators are both correctly null. Neither NC State nor RHS says anything about edibility or pollinators. NC State's only related text is 'ground cover for animals and birds', which names no pollinator. The Missouri Botanical Garden page still fails with ProxyError and 0 bytes, as the researcher reported. RHS gives Max Height 1.5-2.5 m, which differs from NC State, but NC State takes priority as the size source.
